articles.title: Coronal Plane Alignment of the Knee Type I knees are not a homogeneous phenotype : differences in coronal alignment sensitivity following total knee arthroplasty.
articles.authors: Kawaguchi K, Yamagami R, Kono K, Young SW, Tay ML, Taketomi S, et al.
articles.population: Patients undergoing primary total knee arthroplasty using navigation with mechanical alignment strategy
articles.outcomes: Knee Injury and Osteoarthritis Outcome Score (KOOS) at one year; associations between coronal alignment changes and clinical outcomes
articles.take_home: CPAK Type I knees are not all the same. In knees with mild varus deformity, keeping the joint line angle similar to the original anatomy during knee replacement surgery led to better outcomes, but this did not matter as much in knees with severe varus deformity.

articles.title: Clinical outcomes following flexor hallucis longus tendon transfer with and without suture bridge reattachment for insertional Achilles tendinopathy in professional football players.
articles.authors: Batista JP, Yokoe T, Abdelatif NMN, Kamei N, Teramoto A, Takao M, et al.
articles.population: Professional football players with insertional Achilles tendinopathy
articles.outcomes: AOFAS and VAS pain scores, revision surgery rate, return to football and performance level
articles.take_home: All professional football players who had flexor hallucis longus tendon transfer for Achilles tendon problems were able to return to football at nearly the same level as before their injury. Three out of 16 players who had the keyhole surgery approach needed further surgery.

articles.title: Occupational radiation dose surveillance and radiation-protection compliance in podiatric surgery facilities: A nationwide cross-sectional study in Spain.
articles.authors: Cobo-Najar M, Alcaraz M, Achel DG, Pardo-Rios M, Garcia-Gamuz JA, Olivares-Rueda A
articles.study_type: Cross-sectional multicentre survey with on-site dose measurements
articles.population: Podiatric surgery facilities in Spain using fluoroscopy
articles.sample_size: 55 facilities completed questionnaire; 33 underwent on-site inspection
articles.outcomes: Radiation-protection knowledge, compliance with safety protocols, estimated occupational radiation doses to thorax, gonads, eye lens, and hands
articles.take_home: Podiatric surgeons had good theoretical knowledge of radiation safety but poor practical compliance, with none using personal dosimeters or protective equipment during procedures. Although measured doses remained within legal limits, the lack of monitoring means actual exposure is unknown, and better use of protective equipment and safety practices is needed.

articles.title: Normalized tibial sesamoid station on weight-bearing anteroposterior radiographs: Definition, reliability and association with hallux valgus severity.
articles.authors: Bowirrat A, Mahamid MK, Khatib M, Qawasmi F, Robinson D, Eisa M, et al.
articles.population: Patients with hallux valgus undergoing surgery
articles.sample_size: 325 feet from 181 patients (46 patients for reliability testing)
articles.outcomes: Tibial sesamoid station on weight-bearing X-rays; reliability of measurement; association with hallux valgus angle
articles.take_home: Researchers developed a new objective way to measure sesamoid bone position on X-rays that is reliable and reproducible. This measurement is linked to how severe hallux valgus is, beyond what existing measurements show.
